newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish external reserves up 308 mln punts in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Irish external reserves up 308 mln punts in Oct.

text.p: Ireland's official external reserves rose by 308 million punts to 6.030 billion in October, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.
"Positive foreign-exchange market intervention and EU receipts exceeded interest and principal payments on the Exchequer foreign debt," it said in a statement.
The central bank said the money market moved into surplus in October, reflecting the fall in government balances at the central bank and positive foreign exchange market interventions.

"At end-October the bank was absorbing 567 million punts from the market, as discretionary deposits of credit institutions with the bank exceeded liquidity supplied through sale and repurchase agreements," it said.

The central bank said government credit advanced by domestic credit institutions fell by 210 million punts in October as a fall in credit from banks exceeded a modest increase from other credit institutions.
Banks reduced their holdings of government bonds by 257 million punts while other credit institutions increased theirs by 93 million, it said.
Non-resident holdings of Irish securities fell 14 million punts during the month.

"Government balances at the central bank fell by 773 million reflecting the impact of negative Irish-pound funding, net government expenditure and interest and principal payments on the Exchequer foreign debt," the central bank said.
